# Release notes for developers

Changes that affect how you build against PrimeThink: the REST API, the CLI, Live Apps, agents, capabilities and tools, and group and channel configuration. Grouped by the week the work shipped, newest first.

For changes an end user of the app would notice, see the [user release notes](/Release-notes/).

### **Week of October 26, 2026**

**CLI**

* `pt events` and `pt wait` no longer go silently quiet when a connection stays up but stops delivering. Failed room joins are retried, and every `--resync` seconds (5 minutes by default) both commands rejoin and catch up over REST, so `pt wait --pending` still returns unread items the live connection missed. For loops, a finite `--timeout` such as 900 is recommended over 0. It ships in **CLI 1.8.1**.

### **Week of October 19, 2026**

**REST API**

* **A credential reaches only its own group's chats.** A session or API key now reaches only the chats of the group it was issued for: a chat in another group answers `404` even when the key's owner is a member, and the same applies to real-time chat subscriptions and Live App launches. `POST /chats/direct_users` returns a per-group conversation and creates new ones only between exactly two people (`400` otherwise).
* **Inbox.** `GET /api/v1/inbox` gathers unread chats, notifications and message reminders into one newest-first feed, and `GET /api/v1/inbox/counts` returns its badge counts, including mentions, unread messages and overdue reminders. `POST /api/v1/inbox/mark-read` marks the inbox read, optionally narrowed to mentions, and `POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/mark_unread` marks a chat unread.
* **Message reminders** are now kept, so you can list them (`GET /api/v1/chats/reminders`) and cancel one before it fires. A fired reminder stays in the inbox as overdue until you complete it (`POST …/reminders/{id}/complete`) or move it (`PATCH …/reminders/{id}`).
* Messages can carry their author's name and avatar with `include_author=true`, and `GET /api/v1/chats/{chat_id}/messages/{message_id}` returns a single message.
* Error messages now include **`error_summary`**, a short description of what went wrong with no stack trace, credentials, URLs or file paths, in the message API and the real-time `message` event.
* The chat fields `search_in_agent` and `search_in_workspace`, and their `PUT /chats/{id}/search_in_agent` and `PUT /chats/{id}/search_in_workspace` endpoints, are removed. AutoRAG (`search_in_documents`, with `documents_and_collections_enabled`) now covers the documents and collections of the chat, its workspace and its agents; with AutoRAG and Search in Chat Messages both off, nothing is searched automatically. In chat and task settings the **Search in Chat Messages** switch is now labelled **Auto Search in Chat Messages**; the `search_in_chat` field is unchanged.
* Chat message search (`GET /chats/chat_semantic_search_messages`) now searches one chat or workspace you are a member of, chosen by `chat_id` or `chat_uuid`, which is required. A `collection_name` is ignored.
* Workspace endpoints, including creating a chat inside a workspace, now answer `404` to anyone who is neither the workspace's creator nor a member of it.
* Stopping a streaming response now requires access to its chat: the REST endpoint needs a signed-in member of the chat, and anything else answers `404`.
* `GET /collections` returns **`documents_count`** for each collection: the number of documents in it, folders not counted.
* A socket that receives a replayed `agent_responding` event when it joins a chat now always receives that response's end event too; the two may arrive in either order.

**Live Apps**

* Live Apps can stream realtime speech-to-text to OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` as well as ElevenLabs. `pt.sttStreamToken({ provider: 'openai' })` returns a short-lived client secret and WebSocket URL, using the `OPENAI_API_KEY` set as a user or group variable. The session has no server-side turn detection, so the app commits each spoken turn itself. Calls with no options still return an ElevenLabs token. The same token is available over REST at `POST /api/v1/voice/stt/stream/token/openai`.
* `pt.stopStreamingMessage()` now only stops responses in the Live App's own chat.
* In the browser, a trackpad pinch over a Live App no longer zooms the host page. The app still receives those wheel events, so it can implement its own pinch-zoom.
* The Live App editor no longer has a **Content** (canvas HTML) tab; a Live App's files are built and deployed with the agent or `pt`. **Documents** now comes right after **Agents** in the task and Live App editor.

**Agents & capabilities**

* **Z.ai GLM 5.3** is selectable through Mistral as `mistralai:zai-glm-5-3`, using your `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. It is a text-only reasoning model.
* In the agent editor, changing an agent's type now keeps the selected capabilities the new type also supports, and adds the new type's defaults, instead of resetting the selection.
* The agent sandbox now ships **CLI 1.8.0**, so agents working in a sandbox have `pt inbox`, `pt events`, `pt wait` and the new `pt collection create` options.

**CLI**

* **`pt login` signs the CLI in through the browser.** You approve a short code in the web app, signed in however your account signs in, and the CLI receives an API key for each group you pick (90 days by default), saved as a profile named after the group. Use `--no-browser` over SSH or in containers. Logging in again renews the keys and revokes the ones they replace, which needs the Revoke API Keys permission in the group. See [PrimeThink CLI](/developer/PrimeThink-CLI/).
* **`pt inbox`** shows your unread notifications and the chats with unread messages in one call (`--with-messages N` adds each chat's latest unread messages), and `pt chat mark-read` clears a chat. MCP clients get `get_inbox` and `mark_chat_read`. `pt notification list --unread-only` no longer returns every notification, read or not.
* **`pt events`** streams real-time events as JSON lines instead of polling: notifications, unread-count changes and chat updates from every group you belong to, and with `--chat` that chat's messages and agent replies. After each connect and reconnect it first catches up over REST, so a listener that lost its connection still learns what it missed.
* **`pt wait`** blocks until the next matching event, prints it and exits (124 when `--timeout` passes first), which suits scripts and agent loops. `--pending` returns at once while something is unread, and `--after-message-id` waits for the reply to a message you just sent. MCP clients get the same through the `wait_for_event` tool.
* `pt search messages` follows the search change above: it needs `--chat-id`.
* The CLI now writes its config file, which holds your API keys, readable only by you and in one atomic step, so a crash or two commands saving at once can no longer truncate it. A file written by an older version keeps its permissions until the CLI next saves it.
* All of these ship in **CLI 1.8.0**, together with the collection options of the week before.

### **Week of October 12, 2026**

**REST API**

* **API keys are accepted only in the `Authorization: Token` header.** A key passed as an `?api_key=` query parameter is ignored and the request is refused as unauthenticated.
* API keys, sessions and token refreshes for a group stop working (`401`) as soon as their owner is no longer a member of that group.
* Roles are now scoped to their group: another group's custom role answers `404`, system roles can only be changed by a platform Super Admin, and reading a role other than your own needs the view-roles permission.
* Every endpoint that takes an agent id for a chat, task, chat member or your default agent now answers `404` for an agent you cannot use, exactly like an id that does not exist; a reply or replacement must point at a message in the same chat.
* New **`GET /api/v1/settings/known`** lists the setting names the platform reads, with a description and whether each should be stored as a private value. The variable editor uses it to suggest names as you type, along with the names defined at broader levels; a tag such as "Overrides group" marks a name that would take precedence over another level's value.
* Chat links take the form `https://app.primethink.ai/g/<group>/chats/<uuid>`, where `<group>` is the group's name. The older `/chats/<uuid>` form still works.
* `only_visited=true` on the chat list now includes sub-chats the caller opened.
* Adding members through the chat members endpoint now notifies each new member; the notification's metadata carries `kind` (`chat`, `workspace` or `live_app`) and `inviter_user_id`. Opening a chat marks its message-less notifications as read.
* PDF and DOCX output, from message export and from documents saved as PDF or DOCX, now embeds only inline `data:` images; images and other resources referenced by URL or file path are dropped.
* `POST /voice/stt` now transcribes with OpenAI's `gpt-transcribe` instead of `whisper-1`; `POST /voice/translate` still uses `whisper-1`.
* **Long recordings can be diarized in the background.** `POST /voice/diarize/jobs` takes the same files and parameters as `POST /voice/diarize` and answers `202` with a job id, and `GET /voice/diarize/jobs/{job_id}` reports progress and, once completed, the same result body. Jobs are visible only to the user who started them and are kept for 7 days. The mixed audio of a two-microphone recording is now saved as mono 64 kbps MP3, about a third of its previous size.
* The model catalog now returns each model's `release_date` where known, and `GET /api/v1/catalog/llm/providers`, `/providers/{slug}` and `/models` accept `sort=newest` or `sort=oldest` to order models by it, undated models last. Without `sort` the order is unchanged.

**Tasks & Live Apps**

* Editing a task, in the app, the API or with `pt task update`, now reaches chats launched afterwards without publishing a new version, and an empty canvas in a task version no longer blanks the Live App.
* The right sidebar no longer shows a help panel for an attached `@app/HELP.md`. Build help into the Live App or task itself.

**Agents & capabilities**

* **Agents can reply with rendered HTML.** A fenced ` ```widget ` block in a reply renders directly in the message, with Tailwind utility classes available, sized to its content and following light and dark mode; a ` ```html ` block shows **Code** and **Preview** tabs. Each block runs sandboxed and cannot reach the app, the session or the PrimeThink API. Ask for them in an agent's Reply Instructions; see [Rich Replies](/admin/Agents/#rich-replies-widget-and-html-blocks).
* **Gemini 4 Argon** is selectable as `google_genai:gemini-4-argon` and `openrouter:google/gemini-4-argon`. It takes a `reasoning_effort` of `low`, `medium` or `high` and does not accept a temperature. `google_genai:gemini-3.7-flash` and `google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash` are deprecated and no longer listed, but still resolve; the OpenRouter routes of the same models are unchanged.

**CLI**

* `pt collection create` takes `--indexed` and `--ocr-instructions`, so a collection can be made searchable when it is created instead of with a follow-up `pt collection update`. The MCP and agent `create_collection` tools take the same options.

### **Week of October 5, 2026**

**REST API**

* Chat RAG, both automatic and the `rag_search_documents_and_collections` tool, now also searches the indexed collections attached to the chat's agents and the agents' own documents, including in public chats that run those agents.
* Clearing a group's embeddings index no longer deletes its Chat DB and DB Collection data, and that data alone no longer blocks changing the group's embeddings model.
* Saving a long two-microphone diarization with its mixed audio into a collection no longer fails with a closed-connection error.

**Agents & capabilities**

* **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** is selectable as `deepseek:deepseek-flash` (or `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`); DeepSeek V4 Flash is deprecated but still answers. DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4.1 Flash accept a `reasoning_effort` of `low`, `high` or `max`, defaulting to `high`.
* **GPT-6 Astra** accepts a `reasoning_effort` of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max` (not `none`), and reports `medium` as its default in the model catalog.
* OpenRouter gains routes for Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.8 Flash, Grok 4.7, Mistral Large 4 and Muse Spark 1.3. `qwen/qwen3.8-max` now runs as `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902`; agents saved with the old name keep resolving.
* AWS Bedrock gains Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna, and Mistral Large 3. The GPT-6 models and Fable 5.1 need a US region in `AWS_BEDROCK_CREDENTIALS`, Sonnet 5.5 a US or European one, and Fable 5.1 an AWS account whose data-retention mode is `aws_review`; Mistral Large 3 is not offered in Europe.
* The agent sandbox now ships **CLI 1.7.1**, so `pt suite install` run by an agent inside a sandbox no longer stops when the account cannot create tags.

### **Week of September 28, 2026**

**REST API**

* Agents carry a **`reasoning_effort`** setting: one of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`, or empty for the provider's default. It is accepted when creating or updating an agent and returned on every agent response. **`GET /api/v1/catalog/llm/models`** now lists, for each model, `reasoning_efforts` (the levels it accepts, least to most reasoning; empty means the model has no selectable level) and `default_reasoning_effort` (what the provider applies when none is sent, when known). A level the model does not accept is refused with `422` naming the levels it does. On update, leaving the field out keeps the stored level, **an empty string clears it**, and changing the model to one that does not take the stored level clears it for you. A level the model cannot take at run time, for example through a task's model override, is ignored and the provider default is used, so a run does not fail. On Claude, a level switches on extended thinking, which means **`temperature` is no longer sent** for that agent.
* Model registry: **Claude Sonnet 5.5** is selectable through Anthropic directly, as `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`, and **GPT-6.1 Sol** as `openai:gpt-6.1-sol`. Neither accepts a temperature. Sonnet 5.5, like Opus 5.5, does not support computer use; GPT-6.1 Sol is a reasoning model with vision that reads PDFs by extracting their text. Sonnet 5.5 is not yet offered through Bedrock or OpenRouter. Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Sol remain available.
* **A message can now be sent with files and no text.** Posting only attachments to a chat's messages endpoint is accepted and stored as a message with empty text. A request with neither text nor files is refused with `400`. The interactive API reference now shows a file picker for multi-file upload fields.
* `POST /api/v1/public/chats/{chat-id}/public-session` creates the visitor's session again. After the previous release, every first message on a public chat or an embedded live-chat widget was answered with "Parent chat not found"; nothing about the request or response changed. A public visitor is still never required to be a member of the parent chat, but the parent must still belong to the same group as the chat's collections.
* **Chats now remember when you last opened them.** Opening a chat (`GET /api/v1/chats/{chat-id}`) records a visit for the caller, and every item in `GET /api/v1/chats` carries `last_visited_at` (empty until the chat is first opened; existing chats start empty). Add `only_visited=true` to list just the chats the caller has opened, most recently opened first — this replaces the normal ordering, including pinned chats first and manual order.
* **The diarization endpoint can name what it saves.** Three optional parameters are accepted on the query string. `document_name` replaces the uploaded file's name as the base name of the saved documents; `generate_title` adds a short AI-written title and a two-to-three sentence summary, based on the opening of the transcript; and `title_hint` gives the title some context, such as a calendar event's name. The saved documents are called `<name> - transcript.md` and `<name> - audio.mp3`, the transcript opens with its name and the summary, and the response gains `title`, `summary` and `name`. If the title cannot be produced the transcription still succeeds and falls back to `document_name`. Callers that send none of the three see no change.

**Live Apps**

* Filtering by `id` now works. `filters: { id: 42 }` used to look for a field named `id` inside the stored data and so matched nothing; it now matches the entity's own id, on both ChatDB and DB Collections. `id` and `creator_user_id` also accept `$in`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt` and `$lte`, and ids sent as digit strings are accepted. A value that is not a whole number matches nothing, except `$ne`, which then matches every row.
* **Merge edits on a DB Collection work again.** `pt.db(name).edit(id, data, true)` and the `db_edit` action with `merge: true` were failing with a server error on collection rows; they now update only the fields you send and keep the rest, and `ifUnchangedSince` still reports a conflict when the row changed in between. Replace-style edits and ChatDB were not affected.
* A Live App's unread count is now its unread notifications for the viewer, not its chat messages; messages in a Live App chat, including hidden, thinking and tool-call ones, no longer change it. Opening the Live App marks all its notifications read and sends the badge update, including when the count reaches zero. Other chat types still count unread messages.

**Agents & capabilities**

* **Agent types are now enabled per group.** A group can create and run only agents whose type is enabled for it. The list of types returned to you, and `pt agent types`, shows only your group's enabled types; creating an agent, switching its type, or importing a shared agent of a type that is not enabled is refused with `422`, copying agents into a group skips the ones that are not enabled, and an existing agent whose type is not enabled for its group does not run, answering "This agent type is not enabled for this group". Every existing group was set up with the types its agents already use, plus ReAct and Deep, so nothing stops working; new groups start with ReAct and Deep. Adding an agent to a group no longer enables its type. Cloning a task skips agents of a type that is not enabled, and importing a task package falls back to an enabled type.
* **A new agent type, Claude Code, runs the Claude Code CLI in the agent's persistent sandbox** and streams its work into the chat, tool calls included. It brings its own tools and does not use the platform's capabilities, RAG or memory. It is not enabled for any group by default; a platform administrator enables it per group. It needs its own credential, an Anthropic API key or a Claude subscription token, set as a variable on the chat, workspace, user or group, and never uses the platform's keys. Anyone who can message such an agent can make it reveal the credential in use, so give it a variable you do not mind sharing with every member who can run it.

**CLI**

* **`pt suite` installs a whole working set from one package.** A `.ptsuite` package — a folder, a zipped file, a GitHub repository or a catalog entry — holds Live Apps, tasks with schedules, agents, custom capabilities, collections, tags and a workspace, and `pt suite install` creates all of it in one step. It plans first (`--dry-run` only reads), stops before writing anything if a prerequisite is missing, and installing again upgrades in place: it never deletes a collection or removes a capability from an agent, and `--reschedule` re-times schedules after a daylight-saving change. `pt suite uninstall` removes only what the install created, `pt suite export` turns live tasks and Live Apps into a package, and `pt suite build`, `validate`, `inspect` and `catalog` build, check and browse packages. See [Suite Packages](/developer/PrimeThink-CLI/#suite-packages). It ships in **CLI 1.7.0**, the version now baked into the agent sandbox.
* Inside the agent sandbox, the preinstalled `pt` CLI is now signed in automatically: the sandbox's credentials are also exposed as `PRIMETHINK_TOKEN` and `PRIMETHINK_API_URL`, so an agent can run `pt` commands there without setting up a profile.
* **Capability codes now resolve beyond the first ten.** `pt capability resolve` and `pt agent create --capability` read every page of the capability list, so internal codes such as `chat_db_edit`, `memory` and `web_search` no longer come back unresolved.
* **`pt suite install` no longer stops when your account cannot create tags.** Creating tags is limited to platform administrators, so a group administrator's install used to fail partway. It now warns, skips the missing tags and finishes; re-installing still finds what it created, but those resources lack the package's tag.

### **Week of September 21, 2026**

**REST API**

* Settings now resolve over **four** stored levels instead of two: chat, then workspace, then user, then group, before falling back to the platform's own configuration. A level is skipped when there is no context for it, so a background job with no chat resolves exactly as before. A setting's flags — whether its value is private, whether it may be injected into a sandbox — always come from the row that supplied the winning value.
* Workspace and chat variables have the same endpoints as group variables, under the workspace and the chat respectively, split the same way into managed and not-managed settings. Access needs both the matching permission and the ordinary access check for the container: for a workspace, the owner always and other members only when it is fully shared; for a chat, membership to read and the same rule as editing a chat's name to write. A chat or workspace you are not in answers *not found* rather than *forbidden*. Reading a setting by name never falls through to platform configuration, so it cannot be used to fish for server secrets.
* Eight new permissions come with them — view, create, edit and remove for both `workspace_variables` and `chat_variables`. All are global scope and are seeded into the built-in roles on startup, so there is nothing to migrate.
* **Capability options are the exception to the new levels.** The `${SETTING}` placeholders in a capability's options are resolved when an agent's tools are built, which happens with no chat in hand, so they still resolve over the user and group levels only. Do not expect a chat- or workspace-level variable to override a credential referenced from a capability.
* Creating a chat from a task **and** a parent chat in the same call no longer loses the task's knowledge base. The parent's documents and collections used to replace the task's outright; they are now merged, and a document attached to both is linked once, keeping the task's own attachment.
* Listing or creating task simulations now requires that you own the task, hold a role granted access to it, or are a platform administrator — the rule the other evaluation routes already used. Previously any signed-in user could list any task's simulations by id, which exposes each one's goal, persona, prompt and response. A caller without access gets `403`; a task id that does not exist gets `404` instead of an empty list.
* A simulation result now survives the deletion of its inputs. Deleting the simulator agent used to destroy every grade it had ever produced, and deleting the chat the simulation ran in did the same. Both now leave the result in place; `chat_uuid` is nullable and absent when the transcript is gone. Deleting the task still deletes its simulations.
* A simulation carries an explicit `status` of `queued`, `started`, `finished` or `error`, rather than one inferred from timestamps. **`error` is terminal: poll for `finished` or `error`, not `finished` alone.** A run that fails records the reason, including a run that exceeded its time budget — previously a dead run read as running forever. Scheduled evaluation runs record failure the same way. A worker killed outright still cannot report anything, so a long-`started` run remains worth treating as suspect.
* Documents attached to a task or an agent now report their real `document_status`. The field was always `null` on those listings regardless of the actual state.
* **`GET /api/v1/public/chats/{chat-id}/preview`** describes a public chat before a visitor has said anything — the agent's name, whether uploads are available, the task's greeting, and whether the task speaks first — and creates nothing while doing it. It exists so a public chat page can render on load without minting an anonymous user and an empty sub-chat for everyone who merely opens the link. Defer the session endpoint until the visitor actually sends something. Both endpoints now refuse a link that may not be used before creating anything: `404` for an unknown id, `400` for a chat that was never published, `403` for one that has been archived. Every chat has a shareable id from birth, so an id resolving was never the same as the chat being open to visitors.
* **`GET|POST /api/v1/tasks/{task_uuid}/run`** launches a task and answers `303` to the new chat's live page, so a task is reachable by plain link — an email, an intranet button, a QR code — with no API call and no URL to assemble. It takes the task's **uuid**, not its id, plus optional `workspace_id` and `task_version_number`. Access is the same as the launch endpoint, and the caller still needs a session: this is not a public link. **It is not idempotent despite accepting `GET`** — every request creates another chat, so keep one away from anything that fetches URLs speculatively, such as a prefetcher, a crawler or a link-preview generator.
* **A collection is confined to its own group.** Viewing, editing, copying, deleting or attaching one from another group now reports *not found* rather than *forbidden*, so ids cannot be probed across groups. Three consequences: a **catalog task launched from another group brings none of its collections**, so a Live App that expects a shared store will find nothing attached; duplicating a task into another group **copies** its collections instead of linking the originals, leaving two stores that do not share records; and a chat created with a `parent_chat_id` requires the parent to be in the same group with the caller a member of it. Cross-group links already in the database are not removed, only prevented from here on.
* **Deleting a DB Collection now deletes its rows.** They used to outlive the collection, in every group that held any. Deleting one is therefore a data deletion rather than an unlinking, and it takes the records away from every attached chat at once — detach instead when you only want one chat to stop using it.
* **Replies from the GPT-5 and GPT-4.1 families can now be much longer.** When a caller sets no limit of its own, the request carries the model's real maximum output rather than a conservative default — 128K instead of 16K on GPT-5.x, 32K instead of 8K on GPT-4.1. Budget for the longer responses and the cost that comes with them, or set a limit explicitly.
* Model registry refresh: **GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna**, **Claude Fable 5.1** and **Opus 5.5**, and **Gemini 3.8 Flash** and **3.7 Flash** are selectable. The GPT-6 family does not accept a temperature. **GPT-4.1 nano is deprecated** ahead of its October shutdown and no longer appears in model listings; the default for small utility calls has moved to GPT-5.6 Luna, which is a reasoning model and therefore slower than nano was. **Claude Opus 4.1** is deprecated on Anthropic's own API and remains only on Bedrock. Opus 5.5 does not support computer use. A deprecated model disappears from listings but does not disturb an agent already configured with it, so audit your agents rather than waiting for a failure.

**Live Apps**

* `pt.documentUrl(uuid)` builds the URL for displaying or downloading a stored document. Use it for an `<img src>` or an `<a href>` instead of `pt._getUrl()` with a hand-written path — which is what every image-bearing app was doing, against a private method whose path can change. Pass the document's **uuid**, not its integer id; anything that is not a non-empty string throws immediately rather than producing a URL that 404s at render time. Note that the uuid is the access control: that URL streams the file without checking the viewer's session, so treat one like a signed URL.
* `pt.db()` now accepts a collection's numeric **id** as well as its name — `pt.db(42)` alongside `pt.db('project-db')`. An id is the only unambiguous reference when two attached collections share a name, and the only stable one if a collection is later renamed. The REST and action payloads accept `collection_id` beside `collection_name`; when both are sent they must identify the same collection, and a mismatched pair fails to resolve rather than quietly preferring one. An unknown reference reports which collections *are* attached, with their names and ids. Read-only access applies identically to both forms.
* Three constraints worth knowing, each of which has cost someone real work:
    * `hidden: true` on a message hides the **assistant's reply as well as your prompt**. That is usually what you want, but it means a stalled stage of a hidden multi-stage flow leaves nothing at all on screen to explain why the app stopped. Record stage state in ChatDB and show progress in your own interface rather than relying on the transcript.
    * Uploading a file under a name that already exists **in the same folder replaces it** as a new version. Phone cameras hand every capture the same filename, so a user attaching three photos can end up with one document and no error. Generate a unique name per upload when a user can supply more than one file.
    * `pt.list()` has **no sort parameter**, so the order rows arrive in is not a guarantee. Sort explicitly on a field you control. Anything depending on sequence — a streak, a "most recent", a running total — is wrong if it trusts the array order.
* **ChatDB and DB Collections now share one filter implementation**, so every operator behaves identically on both. This settles the two divergences that had their own workarounds: `filters: { done: true }` matches a stored boolean, and a range over an ISO date string works. Data you stored as `'yes'`/`'no'` strings or epoch milliseconds to get around those still filters correctly and needs no migration.
* **Several operators on one field are now AND-ed, on both stores.** `{ age: { $gte: 18, $lt: 30 } }` is a genuine range; previously only the first operator applied and the rest were dropped silently, including inside an `$or` group. Code that compensated by applying one bound in the app is still correct but now filters twice; **code that relied on the extra operators being ignored will start returning fewer rows.** Two smaller changes came with it: `$in: []` matches nothing instead of failing the whole query, and an empty operator object such as `{ age: {} }` is refused with a `400` instead of erroring at `500`.
* Two range behaviours worth knowing, unchanged but easy to trip over: **quoting a number turns the comparison into a text one**, where `"10"` sorts below `"5"`, and a numeric range **skips rows whose stored value is not a number** rather than failing, so one stray `"n/a"` no longer aborts the query but does drop that row.

**Agents & capabilities**

* A new `view_image` tool in the `documents` capability lets an agent actually see an image document from the chat, rather than read its usually-empty extracted text. A viewed image is **pinned** and re-attached on later turns, capped at five per chat with the oldest evicted first; `unpin` releases one. Anything that cannot be shown — not in this chat, not an image, bytes unreadable — comes back as plain text rather than failing the turn. Behaviour is the same across model providers.
* Images on recent messages reach the model within a budget — six images and 15 MB by default, newest first. Past that an image degrades to its metadata rather than erroring, so the model knows the file is attached but can no longer see it. This matters for an app that re-attaches photographs at each stage of a flow: have the agent open a specific image deliberately instead of assuming it is still inside the history budget.
* `read_content_of_url` fetches directly first and can now fall back to a hosted page fetcher when a site refuses the request or serves a page with no readable content in it — the case large retail and marketplace sites hit constantly. `WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER` selects `Auto` (the first of Tavily, Firecrawl, Jina, Serper you have a key for), a specific provider, or `None`; `WEB_FETCH_STRATEGY` is `fallback` by default, or `always` to prefer the provider's extraction on every page. Keys go in your variables as usual, and Tavily's and Serper's are shared with web search. Addresses that are not publicly routable are never sent to a provider. Failures now say what went wrong — the status returned, a timeout, a certificate failure, too many redirects — and a long page is returned in sections rather than truncated.

**Sandbox**

* Sandboxes are no longer Daytona-only. `SANDBOX_BACKEND` selects `daytona` (the default, unchanged) or `kubernetes`, which runs sandboxes in the same cluster as PrimeThink with no external provider. An unrecognised value is rejected rather than falling back silently. The tool, its parameters, the in-sandbox environment, the preinstalled tooling and the security model are identical on both; the settings that were Daytona-specific are now separated from the ones both honour, and the Kubernetes namespace and template are group-overridable while cluster credentials are not. **Computer Use always runs on Daytona** regardless of this setting, so a group using the Kubernetes backend still needs Daytona credentials for it. Selecting `kubernetes` only works where the platform operator has installed the in-cluster components.

**Task evaluation**

* `pt task --help` now points at `pt eval`, where the evaluation and simulation commands actually live. Reading the task help and stopping there previously suggested no evaluation CLI existed at all.

**CLI**

* Scaffolding a Live App into a directory whose name describes a *slot* rather than an app — `sandbox`, `app`, `apps`, `src`, `dist`, `web`, `client`, `frontend` — now takes its name from the parent directory instead. Scaffolding at `word-painter/sandbox` produces "Word Painter", not "Sandbox". Repositories that keep each app's source in a fixed subfolder were titling every app after the subfolder, which is easy to miss until it is the browser tab title of a published app.
* Installing the developer skill now writes a `VERSION` file recording the ref, source and file count, and prints where it went. Quote it when reporting a problem with the skill — without it there is no way to tell which revision produced the behaviour. Writing it is best effort and never fails an otherwise good install.
* **`pt chatdb` can reach a DB Collection.** `list`, `get`, `add`, `update` and `delete` take `--collection NAME` or `--collection-id N` to work on a DB Collection attached to the chat instead of the chat's own store; give both and they must identify the same collection. An id is the unambiguous form when two attached collections share a name, and the stable one across a rename. `pt chatdb init` takes no target — it initialises the chat's own store, and a DB Collection needs no initialisation. The matching MCP tools take the same two parameters. Note that the agent's own Chat DB tools are still **name-only**, so unique names inside a chat still matter.
* **`pt collection create --type db`** creates a DB Collection, which previously needed a direct REST call because the CLI's type list left `db` out. `pt collection update` accepts it too. The four types are `collection`, `skill`, `external_source` and `db`.
* All of the above ships in **CLI 1.6.0**, which is also the version baked into the sandbox snapshot — so an agent working in a sandbox has a `pt` that can target DB Collections.

**Group administration**

* **The All and Unread chat tabs are no longer controlled by a role.** They now appear together, decided by the group's mode: a group presenting itself as a single app hides both, every other group shows both. `show_all_chats_tab` and `show_chats_with_unread_messages_tab` still exist and can still be granted, but nothing reads them. The combination they allowed was unworkable — a member who could see workspaces but had been denied the All tab could not get back out of a selected workspace, stranding them away from every chat belonging to no workspace. Configure the group's mode instead.
* Variables can now be managed from the app at all four levels, using the same editor: user and group on their own **Variables** page, workspace and chat on a Variables tab in each. The tab appears only where the role grants a read of that level, writing is gated separately, a `View Only` workspace shows nothing to anyone but its owner, and a direct message has no chat variables at all. `UI_HIDE_DESKTOP_LINK` is a new UI setting that hides the **Desktop** entry from the user menu; note its sense is inverted relative to the other `UI_` settings — leaving it unset shows the entry.

**Live App templates**

* The React starter derives its **own preview port** per project instead of every scaffold sharing one. With a shared port, a second project's browser suite could adopt a preview server left running by a different app and test that instead — passing while proving nothing, or failing against another app's markup. An already-running preview is no longer reused by default: each run builds and serves this project, and an occupied port fails loudly. `PT_REUSE_PREVIEW` opts back into reuse while iterating and `PT_PREVIEW_PORT` moves off a collision.
* The starter ships **one canonical browser `pt` stub**, replacing the divergent stubs four projects each wrote for themselves. It is backed by session storage, so *write, reload, assert it is still there* is testable — a check an app holding its state in component state fails. It throws on any method it does not implement instead of returning nothing, so it cannot teach an API that does not exist. Use it for rendering and flow only, never as evidence about platform behaviour.
* A separate script loads the built app the way PrimeThink serves it, against a real chat, and asserts that the injected `pt` is real, that the app renders, and that a written row survives a reload. Run it before concluding an app works.
* The shipped table and modal primitives now carry **no palette colours and no dark-mode variants**, taking their colour from CSS variables a project repoints once. This is because overriding one Tailwind colour utility with another is decided by **alphabetical order**, not by intent: `bg-card` beats `bg-white` but loses to nothing in `bg-slate-100`, nothing warns you, and renaming a token can silently flip the result. Two related traps are documented alongside it — a token named after a Tailwind keyword shadows a real utility, and an undefined token emits no CSS at all.
* The first browser-test run fails by design, writing the screenshot baselines it had nothing to compare against. Review the images, commit them, run again.

### **Week of September 14, 2026**

**REST API**

* An API key's role is now checked when the key is created. Ask for no role and the key gets yours; a Group Admin can assign any role in their group except Super Admin and any role holding permissions they do not hold themselves. A key can never be more privileged than the person who created it.
* Task evaluation and simulation runs now have their own, much longer job timeout. A large evaluation plan that used to be cut short by a generic three-minute limit runs to completion.
* Memories are versioned rather than overwritten. Each carries a `status` of `active` or `superseded`, and a superseded row points at the memory that replaced it with the time and, optionally, the reason. Changing a memory's text supersedes it; changing only its priority edits in place. Superseded rows are excluded from listings, search and prompt injection by default — `include_superseded` on the list and search endpoints brings them back, `GET /memories/{id}/history` returns what a memory replaced, and `POST /memories/{id}/supersede` replaces one while keeping the old statement. Deleting a memory is the only operation that destroys its history. Payloads gain `status`, `superseded_by_id`, `superseded_at` and `supersession_reason`.
* Saving or changing a memory of a rule type — `constitution`, `ai_personal`, `agent_constitution`, `workspace_constitution` — now requires a verbatim quote from the user's own message, checked against what they actually wrote. A rule sourced only from a document, a web page, an image or a tool result is refused. Non-rule types are unaffected.

**Live Apps**

* Each Live App is served with its own web app manifest, so it installs as a separate app — its own identity, start address, scope, window and icon — rather than as a shortcut into PrimeThink. An app's identity is tied to its chat rather than its name, so renaming it does not strand or duplicate an existing install.
* A Live App's icon comes from the image on the task behind it. Any image works as long as each delivered size clears 144 pixels in both dimensions; it does not have to be square. Upload a **PNG** — browsers only accept PNG, SVG or WebP for an installable icon, and a resized image is re-encoded as JPEG, which Chrome silently refuses by not offering to install the app at all.
* Real-time updates now use a WebSocket only, with no HTTP long-polling fallback. Polling could not be made reliable across replicas, and pinning the transport is what makes real-time work for a Live App rendered outside the PrimeThink app's own wrapper. If a network blocks WebSocket upgrades, real-time updates will not arrive rather than degrading to polling.
* A Live App now replaces its own credentials before they expire, and recovers by reconnecting when a connection is refused because they already have. An app open longer than a day — a kiosk, a wall display — used to lose real-time updates permanently and start failing its data calls, recoverable only by reloading. There is nothing to call and nothing to configure.

**Public chat**

* Public chats are now served at `/live/{chat-id}/public`. Links already shared at the old `/public/chats/{chat-id}` address are forwarded to it, carrying their query string, so an existing session and an embedder's `ui_*` overrides both survive. Use the new form in anything you build from here. The session endpoint is unchanged.

**Agents & capabilities**

* Two MCP capabilities on one agent that share a `server_label` no longer break it. Providers reject a tools list with a duplicate label and reject the *whole* request, so such an agent could not answer anything at all. Duplicate labels are now collapsed to the first entry — which means only one of the two configurations is in effect, so give them distinct labels or remove the leftover.
* The platform now ships a first-party tool plugin of its own, exposing PrimeThink's management surface — tasks, agents, capabilities, chats, notifications, workspaces, collections, tags, groups — to an agent as tools. It uses exactly the mechanism an external plugin uses, which makes it the clearest working reference for writing your own.

**Task evaluation**

* `similar` scoring is fixed for long answers. It compares word overlap between the answer and the expected response, and a heuristic meant for long repetitive input was dropping common words from the comparison — collapsing the score for any expected answer from roughly 200 characters up, so faithful answers were marked as mismatches. Note that `similar` compares wording, not meaning: use an evaluator agent when a correct answer might be phrased differently.

**CLI**

* The agent tools plugin now ships inside the CLI wheel behind an `agent-tools` extra, rather than as a separate distribution, so the tools and the client code they use can never be different versions. Install it where agents run; plain installs are unchanged. Uninstall the old standalone distribution first if you have it.
* `--pass-threshold` on evaluation settings is a whole percentage from 1 to 100, not a fraction. It was documented as a 0-1 value and rejected the documented example outright; a fraction now fails at the command line instead of travelling to the API. The matching tools an AI agent calls declare the same bound.
* Scaffolding a Live App now names it after the directory, in both the page title and the package name, and says so. Apps used to ship with the template's own title — which reached production more than once, because a browser tab is the last place anyone looks.

**Live App templates**

* The React starter's build now lints before building and verifies the artifact afterwards, with both steps available on their own. The lint rules cover the PrimeThink mistakes that are easy to make and hard to see at runtime: reading an AI reply from the wrong property, mis-ordering the arguments to a change subscription, treating a list result as wrapped in metadata, persisting to browser storage instead of ChatDB, posting an app-driven message without marking it hidden, calling into the platform from inside a React state updater, and using a component that crashes under the template's React version.
* The starter also ships an acceptance-test skeleton to write your spec into before building the interface, a browser suite covering the host-theme bridge and render health, and a couple of primitives worth reusing rather than rewriting. This is a local suite, distinct from the deployed-app test plans the developer skill runs.

### **Week of September 7, 2026**

**REST API**

* New endpoint for launching a task into a chat, which is what the app does when you open a task: the new chat inherits the task's goal, default agent, settings, documents, collections and scheduled job, and the initial prompt is posted. It accepts an optional workspace as either a numeric id or a UUID, a name, a version, and members. The generic chat-creation route can still launch a task, now with an explicit `task_id` body field alongside the existing query parameter. Launching is governed by whether you may *use* a task, which is wider than being allowed to manage it.
* Uploading a document whose name is already taken now has a defined contract: identical content reuses the existing document, different content replaces it in place and records a new Production version, and an unresolvable conflict answers `409`. This also fixes a `500` when a same-named file was uploaded to a task without a folder — the default for command-line uploads.
* Documents a chat inherits from a task now record where they came from. Chat document and directory listings report the source task and whether that task has since dropped the document, and applying a task update reconciles the inherited files — adding, removing and repointing them — while leaving anything uploaded directly into the chat untouched. The update-check endpoint reports the pending document changes, which is what keeps "update available" honest when only a task's documents changed.
* Archiving moved off the agent *status* field onto a dedicated flag, so an agent can be archived and still active. List endpoints for agents and tasks hide archived entries unless you pass `archived=true`, and agent records carry the flag. The older `status=archived` and `status=all` filters still work and are translated for you; prefer the flag in new code.
* Connection endpoints accept a chat as either a numeric id or a UUID, and check chat membership consistently before anything else.
* Memory is now organized into pages, with an API for reading and writing pages and categories. Atomic memories remain the source of truth — a page is a view over the ones filed under it, and page summaries are derived rather than stored prose. A nightly job files new memories, merges pages describing the same entity, removes duplicates, settles contradictions by recency and rebuilds changed summaries. The stable part of memory is injected with the other per-chat-stable context while query-dependent recall goes at the tail of the prompt, so the volatile block no longer invalidates the cacheable prefix in front of it.

**Agents**

* Three agent types that no longer served a purpose are gone: the plain chat, SQL and summarisation types. Anything still pointing at them needs to move to a remaining type.
* The type formerly called `Std3` is now `ReAct1`. The old name is still accepted and normalised wherever a type is named, so existing configuration keeps working, but expect to see the new name.
* The sandbox agent now receives the chat's goal and its in-context documents in its system prompt, bringing it in line with the other agent types.
* A document lookup by path inside the sandbox now finds files a chat inherited from a task. Those links were created without a per-link name, so by-path resolution could never match them, and pulling such a file into the sandbox failed with "no document found" even though listings showed it.

**Channels (Telegram & Slack)**

* Photos and documents sent to a Telegram bot reach the agent as chat documents, with the caption as the message text and a stand-in prompt when there is none. Downloads are capped at the Bot API's 20 MB and refused politely above it, and the reply policy is evaluated *before* the download, so an attachment in a conversation the bot would not answer is never fetched.
* Documents the assistant attaches to an answer are delivered to the conversation after the text — images inline as photos on Telegram, everything else as a file, and uploads into the reply's thread on Slack. Up to ten per answer, best effort per file, skipping anything over the platform's own limit.
* Slack file uploads need the `files:write` scope, which is in the current manifest. **A Slack app created before that scope was added must be reinstalled from the current manifest**, or its uploads fail while text replies keep working.

**Documents**

* Removing a document link from a chat or a task no longer filters on who originally uploaded it. Authorization is already decided by the route, and the extra filter only produced spurious `404`s: a user who launched someone else's task could not remove the inherited document from their own chat, and a task co-editor could not remove a colleague's upload.

**CLI**

* **1.4.0** closes the gap between the CLI and the API. New command families for audio and video processing, group and member management, tags, chat workspaces, folders and document versions across chats, collections, tasks and agents, message-level operations including export and save-as-task, collection lifecycle and copy, image search within a collection, and listing tasks with filters. Each is mirrored as an MCP tool, with the non-destructive subset exposed to the agent tools plugin.
* **1.4.1** adds notifications, a full task-evaluation flow — build a plan, run it, simulate a multi-turn conversation, read and download results — a generic settings interface over group and user settings including provider keys (which are never read back), a user directory lookup for turning an email into an id, capability *codes* rather than environment-specific ids when creating an agent, agent avatar images, and an active group and configured provider list on `whoami`. Any 2xx now counts as success, so endpoints answering `204` no longer surface as errors.
* **1.5.0** adds launching a task into a chat from the command line, and gives task publishing the task type and feature toggles it never had — on the command line or in an optional `task.json` in the project, with an explicit option winning over the file. Previously a published task was always private with documents, chat history and scheduling off, and no way to say otherwise. Updating an existing task still only changes what your project states.
